claims.text: Adding a minor fraction of La2O3 nanoparticles to CoCrFeNi will enable in situ formation of a lanthanum-rich oxide scale during sliding.
The lanthanum-rich oxide scale will be lubricious.
La2O3 doping will maintain a lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
La2O3 doping will reduce the wear rate relative to undoped CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
The introduced La2O3 nanoparticles will be uniformly dispersed in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Dispersed La2O3 nanoparticles will act as nucleation sites for a protective lanthanum-rich oxide tribolayer.
La2O3 nanoparticles will promote rapid in situ generation of a stable oxide scale under sliding.
The generated oxide scale will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
The generated oxide scale will reduce interfacial shear stresses.
The proposed oxide-scale mechanism will operate effectively across the entire 25–800 °C test regime.
The oxide scale will counteract an increase in friction and wear at elevated temperatures.
The predicted benefit applies in ambient air under dry or lightly humid sliding conditions.
The predicted benefit applies under moderate-to-high contact loads representative of engineering applications.
The reductions in friction and wear may vary with load, temperature gradients, and environmental fluctuations.
A 2–3 wt% La2O3 addition is the proposed experimental implementation of the intervention.
